instructional_purpose: Opens the followers module by naming the four member categories of the تابع class and then developing the descriptive follower in depth. The learner is taught to license an attributive modifier by four simultaneous agreement dimensions and to read a case ending as the signal of which noun inside an annexation chain the modifier attaches to.
concepts_taught: the تابع class and its four members
four-dimension agreement licensing for an attributive modifier: gender, number, case, definiteness
feminine singular agreement forced by a non-human plural head
the elative shape used attributively and its restricted agreement
stacked modifiers, each licensed independently against one head
attachment of a modifier inside an annexation chain resolved by case
the direct descriptive follower versus the causal descriptive follower
attributive modification versus the indefinite circumstantial accusative

linguistic_propositions.proposition: An attributive modifier is licensed only when it matches its head in gender, number, case, and definiteness at once.
A plural head whose referents are non-human licenses a feminine singular modifier regardless of the gender of the corresponding singular.
An elative-shaped modifier stays in its base masculine singular shape and agrees only in case and definiteness.
The elative has distinct feminine shapes only when it stands as a noun, never when it stands as a follower.
Several modifiers on one head are each licensed independently against that head and need no coordinator between them.
After an annexation chain, the case borne by a following modifier identifies which member of the chain it modifies.
In the causal descriptive follower, the modifier takes its gender from the noun that follows it rather than from the head it is attached to.
The descriptive follower encodes a stable property while the circumstantial accusative encodes a transient state, and the two separate by definiteness behaviour.

recognition_criteria: a post-nominal item bearing the same case marker as the immediately preceding noun with no coordinator between them
definiteness parity between the two, which is what separates attribution from a two-term predication
a feminine singular modifier on a plural head, which signals a non-human referent set
an elative-shaped modifier that fails gender or number agreement but still matches case and definiteness
a modifier immediately followed by a noun carrying a possessive clitic that points back to the head, marking the causal type
procedures: read the four features off the head, then copy each onto the modifier
for a plural head, classify referent animacy first, then choose between full plural and feminine singular agreement
inside an annexation chain, choose the modifier case from the intended attachment target
for the causal type, take gender from the following noun and hold the modifier singular
conditions: attribution requires definiteness parity; a definite head with an indefinite following nominal is read as predication instead
the non-human rule is triggered by referent animacy, not by the grammatical gender of the singular
the case-based attachment cue is informative only when the chain members carry different cases
exceptions: the elative resists gender and number agreement in this presentation
the causal descriptive follower breaks gender agreement with its own head
contrasts: human plural versus non-human plural agreement
attachment to the first versus the second member of an annexation chain

common_mistakes.pattern: putting a human masculine plural modifier on a plural head whose referents are things
common_mistakes.why_wrong: animacy, not the gender of the singular, governs plural agreement
common_mistakes.correction_principle: classify referent animacy before selecting any plural agreement form

common_mistakes.pattern: pairing a definite head with an indefinite modifier while intending attribution
common_mistakes.why_wrong: definiteness parity is part of the licensing condition, so the string is read as a predication instead
common_mistakes.correction_principle: match definiteness on both members or accept the predicative reading

common_mistakes.pattern: inflecting an elative for feminine gender when it stands as a follower
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the lesson treats the attributive elative as invariable in gender and number
common_mistakes.correction_principle: hold the elative in its base shape and agree only in case and definiteness

common_mistakes.pattern: assigning the wrong case to a modifier that follows an annexation chain
common_mistakes.why_wrong: case is the only overt attachment signal, so the wrong case silently relocates the modification
common_mistakes.correction_principle: derive the modifier case from the intended attachment target, then check it against the reading

common_mistakes.pattern: labelling an indefinite post-verbal descriptive accusative as a modifier of the preceding noun
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the two differ in definiteness behaviour and in whether the property is asserted as stable or as a state at the time of the event
common_mistakes.correction_principle: test definiteness parity against the preceding noun before assigning the attributive label

misleading_shortcuts: the claim that the case ending always reveals what a modifier attaches to, which fails whenever both chain members carry the same case
the claim that the elative never changes shape, which conflicts with the standard requirement that a definite elative agree with its head
permanent versus temporary as the test separating modifier from circumstantial, which is a rough heuristic and misclassifies stable circumstantials
the statement that the causal modifier agrees with the following noun, which omits that it still takes case and definiteness from the head and stays singular
worked_analysis_stages: identify head and modifier
tabulate the four features of the head
check each feature on the modifier in turn
for annexation chains, name the attachment target and derive the case from it
paradigms: a four-row feature grid contrasting a definite and an indefinite attributive pair
a plural agreement grid with rows for human masculine, human feminine, and non-human heads
a per-dimension table for the elative marking which dimensions agree and which do not
exercise_types: multiple choice on the agreement dimensions
attachment identification after an annexation chain
free response recall of grammatical role names
prerequisite_knowledge: definiteness marking by article versus nunation
definiteness inheritance inside an annexation chain
new_knowledge: the follower class itself and its four members
four-dimension agreement stated as a licensing condition rather than a habit
animacy-conditioned plural agreement
case as an attachment disambiguator after annexation
the causal descriptive follower
later_dependencies: the agreement exceptions lesson that closes this module
sarf_relevance: medium - the rules key off elative, feminine, and plural template shapes although no derivation of those shapes is taught here
nahw_relevance: high - agreement licensing and attachment resolution are core syntactic decisions
tutor_drill_relevance: high - feature copying and attachment items are mechanically checkable once the head features are given, except for the elative items
rich_hover_relevance: high - a hover on a modifier can name the head it attaches to and list the features that licensed it
corpus_pvn_relevance: n - adjectival and elative noun entries; elative-pattern headwords and non-human plural heads are the obvious families; no particle or verb entries are required by this lesson
required_evidence: per-occurrence gender, number, case, and definiteness on both head and modifier; an animacy label on any plural head; and, inside an annexation chain, an annotated attachment target
uncertainty_flags: the invariable attributive elative rule conflicts with the standard agreement requirement for a definite elative and must not be projected onto generated or corrected text
the permanent versus temporary criterion separating modifier from circumstantial is a teaching heuristic, not a decision procedure
feminine plural agreement with lifeless plurals is attested and is not acknowledged anywhere in the lesson

proposed_new_units.summary: Licensing table for the attributive descriptive follower: given head features plus a referent animacy label, it states the required modifier features, and given an annexation chain it states which case realises which attachment, including an explicit undecidable outcome when both chain members share a case.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 assigns case once a slot is known and u-s08 supplies number and gender morphology, but neither states the joint condition under which a following nominal counts as a modifier at all, and u-n10 records attachment and scope without a case-driven procedure for choosing between annexation members.

instructional_purpose: Develops the emphasis follower in its meaning-word variety: a small closed set of nominals placed after a noun to reinforce identity or totality, each obligatorily carrying a clitic pronoun coindexed with the reinforced noun and copying its case, with a separate gendered pair reserved for duals.
concepts_taught: semantic emphasis as one of the four follower types
identity emphasizers versus totality emphasizers
the obligatory coindexed clitic on the emphasizer
case copying from the reinforced noun
substitution of the plural shape of the identity emphasizer with plural heads
the two dual emphasizers كلا and كلتا and their nominative versus oblique shapes
rhetorical force of emphasis in persuasion and in warning

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Semantic emphasis reinforces a nominal without adding any descriptive content, so removing it leaves the proposition intact.
The emphasizer must carry a clitic pronoun agreeing with the reinforced noun in person, gender, and number.
The emphasizer copies the case of the reinforced noun in all three cases.
With a plural reinforced noun the identity emphasizer appears in its plural shape rather than taking a plural clitic on the singular shape.
The dual emphasizers behave as invariable annexation heads before an overt noun and inflect like duals when they carry a clitic.
A dual reinforced noun takes the singular-shaped identity emphasizer with a dual clitic.
A totality quantifier heading an indefinite noun in annexation is an instance of emphasis.
An identity emphasizer standing before the noun it identifies is an instance of emphasis.
The two totality words divide as wholeness of a single entity versus collective inclusion of a set.

recognition_criteria: a post-nominal member of a small closed nominal set
an attached clitic pronoun coindexed with the immediately preceding noun
a case marker identical to that of the preceding noun
no new property is asserted, so deleting the item leaves a complete sentence
for duals, one of the two gendered forms selected by the referent gender
procedures: identify the reinforced noun and read its case and phi-features
select the emphasizer by the intended force, identity or totality
attach the clitic matching person, gender, and number
assign the emphasizer the same case as the reinforced noun
for duals, select the gendered dual emphasizer and then its nominative or oblique shape
conditions: the emphasizer follows the reinforced noun and does not precede it
a clitic is obligatory whenever the emphasizer follows an overt noun
the gendered choice between the two dual emphasizers is fixed by referent gender
every worked example presupposes a definite reinforced noun, but the definiteness condition is never stated
exceptions: plural heads take a different lexical shape of the identity emphasizer rather than a different clitic
the dual emphasizers alternate between annexation-head behaviour and dual inflection depending on what follows
contrasts: emphasis versus description, since emphasis adds no property

common_mistakes.pattern: leaving the emphasizer bare with no clitic
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the coindexed clitic is what links the emphasizer to its head and licenses the construction
common_mistakes.correction_principle: always attach a clitic resolved to the reinforced noun

common_mistakes.pattern: attaching a clitic whose gender does not match the reinforced noun
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the clitic is the agreement carrier, so a gender mismatch breaks the coindexation
common_mistakes.correction_principle: read gender off the reinforced noun before selecting the clitic

common_mistakes.pattern: giving the emphasizer a case different from the reinforced noun
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the follower relation is realised as case identity
common_mistakes.correction_principle: copy the case of the reinforced noun onto the emphasizer

common_mistakes.pattern: using the singular shape of the identity emphasizer with a plural head
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the construction substitutes the plural lexical shape rather than pluralising only the clitic
common_mistakes.correction_principle: switch the emphasizer to its plural shape when the head is plural

common_mistakes.pattern: using the nominative dual emphasizer shape in an accusative or genitive slot
common_mistakes.why_wrong: with a clitic the dual emphasizer inflects like any dual and has a distinct oblique shape
common_mistakes.correction_principle: select the dual shape from the case of the reinforced noun

common_mistakes.pattern: using the masculine dual emphasizer with a feminine dual head
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the two dual emphasizers are lexically specialised by gender
common_mistakes.correction_principle: choose the dual emphasizer by referent gender before considering case

misleading_shortcuts: treating every occurrence of a totality word as emphasis, when in several of the lesson's own illustrations the word is an annexation head with its own case assigned by its clause role
assuming a pre-nominal identity word is emphasis, which contradicts the post-nominal requirement the lesson itself states
reading the wholeness versus collective split between the two totality words as a hard rule rather than a tendency
worked_analysis_stages: locate the reinforced noun
classify the emphasizer as identity or totality
verify the clitic and resolve its referent
verify the case copy
state the rhetorical effect in context
paradigms: a clitic selection table indexed by person, gender, and number of the reinforced noun
a three-case table showing the emphasizer copying each case
a two-row dual paradigm giving the nominative and oblique shapes of both dual emphasizers
exercise_types: completion with the correct clitic form
free response recall of role names
prerequisite_knowledge: dual inflection and its two shapes
the follower class from the preceding lesson
new_knowledge: a closed lexical set that functions only as a follower
an obligatory coindexed clitic stated as a licensing condition
gendered dual emphasizers with two case shapes
plural shape substitution rather than clitic pluralisation
later_dependencies: verbal emphasis, which is defined against this lesson
the resumptive clitic requirement in two apposition types
sarf_relevance: medium - requires the plural shape of the identity nominal and dual inflection, but no derivation is taught
nahw_relevance: high - a follower with an explicit two-part licensing condition, coindexed clitic plus case copy
tutor_drill_relevance: high - clitic selection and case copying are deterministic once the head features are known
rich_hover_relevance: high - a hover can name the reinforced noun and resolve the clitic without ambiguity, provided annexation-head uses are excluded first
corpus_pvn_relevance: n - the emphasizer set is a small closed class of nominals plus the two dual forms; entries need a distinct emphasis-follower sense separate from their ordinary nominal senses
required_evidence: for each candidate, the antecedent noun case and phi-features, the resolved referent of the clitic, and positive evidence that the item is post-nominal rather than an annexation head with independently assigned case
uncertainty_flags: the dual clitic on the singular identity emphasizer is contested; many grammarians prefer the plural shape for duals
quantifier-plus-indefinite structures are labelled emphasis here although they are annexation heads
one illustration places the identity emphasizer before its noun, violating the post-nominal requirement the lesson itself states
the classical emphasizer inventory includes further totality words that this lesson does not present

proposed_new_units.summary: Licensing table for the meaning-word emphasis follower: closed lexical inventory, the obligatory coindexed clitic keyed to head phi-features, case copying, plural shape substitution, and the dual pair with its two case shapes, plus an explicit reject rule for the same lexemes used as annexation heads.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-s09 covers clitic and inflection layering as morphology and u-n01 assigns case per slot, but neither states when a following nominal is licensed as an emphasis follower, and nothing in the catalog separates these lexemes in their follower use from their far more common annexation-head use.

instructional_purpose: Presents the repetition variety of the emphasis follower: reinforcement obtained by repeating a token identically, extended beyond nominals to verbs, particles, and whole clauses, and set explicitly against the meaning-word variety taught in the preceding lesson.
concepts_taught: emphasis by exact repetition as a follower relation
role labels for the repeated and the repeating token
the word classes eligible for repetition, including whole clauses
identity of form, case, tense, person, and number between the two tokens
rhetorical functions attributed to repetition
the boundary between repetition emphasis and coordination of identical items
why verbs are reachable only by this emphasis type

linguistic_propositions.proposition: An immediately repeated identical token stands as a follower to the first token and constitutes emphasis.
The repeating token must match the first in case, form, tense, person, and number.
All word classes may be repeated, including particles and full clauses, unlike meaning-word emphasis which reaches nominals only.
Verbs cannot be reinforced by the meaning-word emphasizers, so repetition is the only available route for them.
Inserting a coordinator between the two tokens changes the analysis from emphasis to coordination.
Any immediate repetition of an identical token is emphasis.
A bare governing particle can be repeated on its own as emphasis.
The rhetorical effects of urgency, insistence, emotional intensity, and confirmation are recoverable from the repetition itself.

recognition_criteria: two adjacent tokens identical in segmental form and in inflection
no coordinator and no pause particle standing between them
the second token introduces no new argument and fills no independent syntactic slot
for clause repetition, the whole clause recurs rather than a fragment of it
procedures: confirm token identity including vowelling
confirm inflectional identity across case for nominals and across tense, person, and number for verbs
assign the emphasized and emphasizer roles by linear order
read the rhetorical effect from the surrounding discourse
conditions: exact form identity is required, not near identity or a synonym
the repeating token follows immediately
clause repetition requires the whole clause
exceptions: a coordinator between the two tokens removes the emphasis reading and yields coordination
meaning-word emphasis is unavailable for verbs, which is why this type carries the whole load there
contrasts: repetition versus coordination of two identical items
reinforcement carried by sound and rhythm versus reinforcement carried by added semantic content
the same repetition device used to warn versus used to intimidate, illustrated from two very different registers

common_mistakes.pattern: repeating a verb in a different tense or a different form
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the construction is licensed by exact identity, so a form change makes the second token an independent predication
common_mistakes.correction_principle: reproduce the first token exactly, including tense, person, and number

common_mistakes.pattern: repeating a nominal with a different case ending
common_mistakes.why_wrong: case identity is the visible mark of the follower relation
common_mistakes.correction_principle: copy the case of the first token onto the second

common_mistakes.pattern: treating repetition emphasis and meaning-word emphasis as one category
common_mistakes.why_wrong: they differ in method, in the word classes they reach, and in what agreement they require
common_mistakes.correction_principle: classify by method first, then apply the agreement rules of that type

common_mistakes.pattern: attempting meaning-word emphasis on a verb
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the meaning-word emphasizers are nominals and take a nominal head
common_mistakes.correction_principle: use repetition for verbs

common_mistakes.pattern: leaving an assertion unmarked where emphasis was intended
common_mistakes.why_wrong: not an error of grammar; the lesson frames it as a loss of the intended rhetorical force
common_mistakes.correction_principle: treat this as a stylistic choice, not a correctness rule

common_mistakes.pattern: inserting a coordinator between the two tokens and still reading emphasis
common_mistakes.why_wrong: with a coordinator the second token is a conjunct and the reading shifts
common_mistakes.correction_principle: check for an intervening coordinator before assigning the emphasis label

misleading_shortcuts: the assumption that any repeated word is emphasis, which the lesson supplies with no filter against false starts, enumeration, vocative repetition, or two genuinely distinct instances
stating exact form identity for verbs while omitting the classical constraint that a governing particle be repeated together with what it governs
presenting rhetorical labels as though they follow from the form, when they are read off the situation
worked_analysis_stages: spot the adjacent identical pair
verify inflectional identity
assign the two role labels by order
classify the rhetorical effect from context
paradigms: a word-class inventory table showing repetition across nominals, verbs, particles, and clauses
a case identity table across the three cases
a verb identity table across tense and across person and number
exercise_types: multiple choice discriminating the two emphasis types
free response recall of role names
fill in the blank with the repeated form
prerequisite_knowledge: verb tense, person, and number morphology
reuses_from_earlier: L4.M2.02 emphasis category and role labels
new_knowledge: repetition treated as a licensed syntactic follower rather than as a stylistic device
extension of emphasis to non-nominals and to whole clauses
the intervening-coordinator test
later_dependencies: coordination, which needs the coordinator versus repetition boundary drawn here
discourse level cohesion and rhetorical analysis
sarf_relevance: low - requires only that the second token be morphologically identical to the first; no derivation or template reasoning is taught
nahw_relevance: medium - a follower relation is asserted, but it carries no case assignment or agreement computation beyond identity
tutor_drill_relevance: medium - identity checks drill cleanly, but the rhetorical effect items are interpretive and are not safely auto-gradable
rich_hover_relevance: medium - a hover can mark the second token as an emphasizer only if false-start, enumeration, and distinct-instance readings have been excluded, which form alone cannot do
corpus_pvn_relevance: p - repeated response and negation particles are the clearest entry candidates; verb and noun entries gain only a usage note here, since no new lexeme is introduced by the construction
required_evidence: adjacency, exact segmental and inflectional identity, absence of an intervening coordinator, and a discourse check that the second token is not an independent instance or a disfluency
uncertainty_flags: no formal filter is offered that separates emphatic repetition from disfluency, enumeration, or vocative repetition
the classical constraint requiring a governing particle to be repeated with its complement is not stated
the rhetorical effect labels are interpretive and cannot be projected from form

proposed_new_units.summary: Decision table for adjacent identical tokens: routes a pair to emphatic repetition, to coordination, or to a no-decision outcome, keyed on the presence of an intervening coordinator, inflectional identity, whether the second token fills an independent slot, and a discourse check for disfluency or enumeration.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-n12 treats cohesion across a discourse, but the question this lesson raises is a local one, namely whether an adjacent identical pair is a licensed follower at all; no catalog unit supplies that reject path, and without it any repetition detector would over-fire.

instructional_purpose: Consolidates coordination as a follower relation and inventories ten coordinating particles sorted by sequencing, alternation, correction versus contrast, negation of the second term only, extreme inclusion, and paired alternation, with case transmitted from the first term to the second throughout.
concepts_taught: coordination as a follower relation with two role labels
case transmission from the first term to the conjoined term
sequencing contrast among the three additive particles
declarative alternation versus interrogative alternation
correction and retraction versus adversative contrast
the coordinator that affirms the first term and negates only the second
the extreme-inclusion coordinator
the paired either construction and its obligatory second member

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The conjoined term takes the same case as the term it is conjoined to, and this holds for every particle in the set.
The three additive particles differ in whether sequence is entailed and whether a delay is entailed.
One alternation particle belongs to statements and the other to alternative questions.
بل cancels or downgrades the first term while لكن leaves it standing and merely contrasts.
لكن coordinates a plain contrast after an affirmative clause.
لا used as a coordinator affirms the first term and negates only the second.
حتى coordinates an extreme member of the set and transmits case to it.
إمّا is itself one of the coordinating particles.
The inventory of coordinating particles numbers exactly ten.

recognition_criteria: a particle from the closed set standing between two units that share a case
case identity between the two units, with no independent governor for the second
an interrogative frame, which selects the question-alternation particle
a preceding negation or prohibition, which licenses the corrective reading
position between two single terms, which separates the coordinating negator from clause negation
procedures: identify the first term and read its case and clause role
select the particle from the intended semantic relation
assign the second term the same case
for the paired construction, supply the second member with its partner particle
conditions: the corrective particle characteristically follows a negation, or upgrades an affirmation
the coordinating negator requires an affirmative first term and single-term conjuncts
the paired construction requires its second member to be present
case transmission applies uniformly across the whole set
exceptions: a coordinator that negates instead of adding
a coordinator that includes an extreme instead of alternating
a member of the set that cannot stand without its partner
contrasts: additive with no sequence versus immediate sequence versus delayed sequence
clause negation versus coordinating negation, separated by position
coordination versus the emphatic repetition of the preceding lesson

common_mistakes.pattern: using the declarative alternation particle inside an alternative question
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the classical division assigns alternative questions to the other particle
common_mistakes.correction_principle: select the alternation particle from the clause type, and note that the lesson itself concedes modern usage is looser

common_mistakes.pattern: reading the coordinating negator as ordinary clause negation
common_mistakes.why_wrong: as a coordinator it stands between two terms, whereas clause negation precedes the predicate
common_mistakes.correction_principle: use position relative to the two terms as the test

common_mistakes.pattern: dropping case agreement on the second term
common_mistakes.why_wrong: case transmission is the formal content of the coordination relation
common_mistakes.correction_principle: copy the case of the first term onto the second

common_mistakes.pattern: using the corrective particle for a plain contrast after an affirmative clause
common_mistakes.why_wrong: correction cancels or upgrades the first term, which is not what a plain contrast asserts
common_mistakes.correction_principle: reserve correction for cancelling or upgrading, and use the adversative for contrast

common_mistakes.pattern: leaving the paired alternation construction with only its first member
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the paired word sets up an alternation that the second member must close
common_mistakes.correction_principle: always supply the second member with its partner particle

misleading_shortcuts: presenting a ten-member inventory as settled when both the count and the membership are disputed in the tradition

glossing لكن simply as but, which hides that as a coordinator it joins single terms after a negation or prohibition, and that the lesson's own repair for the fourth error silently switches to the clause-governing homograph instead
treating the sequencing glosses of the additive particles as entailments enforced in every text rather than as defaults
describing the extreme-inclusion particle by meaning alone, omitting both the condition that the following term belong to the preceding set and the dispute over whether it coordinates at all
worked_analysis_stages: locate the particle
identify the first term, its case, and its clause role
assign case to the second term
classify the semantic relation the particle encodes
paradigms: a ten-row particle table giving meaning and the distinguishing feature of each
a three-case transmission table
a sequencing comparison table for the three additive particles
a two-column correction versus contrast table
exercise_types: free response recall of role names
fill in the blank particle selection
prerequisite_knowledge: an earlier lesson covering the first seven particles
reuses_from_earlier: an earlier coordination lesson covering the first seven particles
new_knowledge: the three less common coordinators, namely the negating, the extreme-inclusion, and the paired one
the declarative versus interrogative split between the two alternation particles
separation of correction from adversative contrast
later_dependencies: apposition and appositional clarification, which must be told apart from coordination
sarf_relevance: low - the particles are uninflected and no morphology is taught
nahw_relevance: high - case transmission and particle licensing are central syntax
tutor_drill_relevance: high for case transmission and for particle selection in clear frames; low for items that turn on disputed membership
rich_hover_relevance: high - almost every form in this set has non-coordinating uses, so per-occurrence sense selection is exactly what a hover must deliver
corpus_pvn_relevance: p - ten particle entries, most of them multifunction: the same forms also serve as clause negation, as a subordinator or goal preposition, as a clause-level adversative, and as an interrogative marker, so each needs per-occurrence sense evidence
required_evidence: the case of both terms, the polarity of the preceding clause, the syntactic size of the second unit (single term versus clause), interrogative framing, and for the extreme-inclusion particle whether the following term belongs to the preceding set
uncertainty_flags: the size and membership of the coordinator inventory is school-dependent
the coordinator status of the extreme-inclusion particle is disputed

proposed_new_units.summary: Per-occurrence discriminator for the coordination particle set: for each form, separates the coordinating use from its homographic non-coordinating uses using position between two terms, case identity, polarity of the preceding clause, and the size of the following unit, with an attributed no-decision path for the two disputed members.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 already establishes the multifunction-particle problem but is scoped to one form; this lesson adds a whole family of forms whose coordinating and non-coordinating senses are distinguished by different evidence, and u-n11 records rival analyses without providing the per-occurrence test.

instructional_purpose: Introduces apposition as the fourth follower: a substitute nominal that carries the syntactic weight of the noun it follows, presented through a four-way typology and a resumptive clitic requirement that holds for exactly two of the four types.
concepts_taught: apposition as a follower and the role label for the substituted-for noun
total apposition where the two nominals are referentially identical
partitive apposition naming a part of the first noun
inclusion apposition naming a quality or aspect of the first noun
corrective apposition replacing a misstatement
case identity between the two nominals
the resumptive clitic required by two types and forbidden in one
apposition contrasted with the descriptive follower

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The appositive carries the same case as the noun it follows.
The appositive is the element the predication actually targets, so the sentence would stand with the first noun removed.
Partitive and inclusion apposition require a clitic pronoun on the appositive that resolves to the first noun.
Total and corrective apposition take no such clitic, because the appositive either is or replaces the first noun.
Partitive apposition covers physical parts while inclusion apposition covers abstract qualities.
Corrective apposition is uncommon in formal writing and is normally replaced by an explicit corrective particle or a metalinguistic phrase.
The four types exhaust the category.

recognition_criteria: a second nominal immediately after the first, with identical case and no coordinator between them
a clitic on the second nominal that resolves to the first, marking the partitive or inclusion type
referential identity with no clitic, marking the total type
no property is predicated of the first noun, which is what separates apposition from description
procedures: confirm case identity between the two nominals
test whether the second nominal alone would carry the predication
check for a clitic and resolve its antecedent
classify as identity, part, quality, or correction
conditions: adjacency with no coordinator intervening
a resumptive clitic is obligatory in the two connected types
in the total type the appositive must itself be able to bear the predication
exceptions: the corrective type discards the first nominal instead of clarifying it
no clitic appears where the two nominals are referentially identical
contrasts: total versus partitive versus inclusion versus corrective apposition

common_mistakes.pattern: omitting the clitic in the partitive or inclusion type
common_mistakes.why_wrong: without the clitic there is no formal link back to the first nominal, and the pair reads as a different construction
common_mistakes.correction_principle: attach a clitic that resolves to the substituted-for noun

common_mistakes.pattern: assigning a part reading where a quality reading is intended, or the reverse
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the two types are distinguished by whether the appositive is a genuine portion of the first noun or something the first noun merely bears
common_mistakes.correction_principle: ask whether the appositive could be separated from the whole before choosing the type

common_mistakes.pattern: giving the appositive a case different from the first nominal
common_mistakes.why_wrong: case identity is the formal signature of the follower relation

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Appositional clarification agrees in case with the nominal it clarifies.
It explains rather than substitutes, so the first nominal remains the primary reference.
It is formally indistinguishable from total apposition; only intended emphasis separates them.
A two-way deletion test decides which of the two labels applies.
Some grammarians treat it as a subtype of apposition rather than an independent category.
The three positions in the dispute align with the Basran school, the Kufan school, and a later contextual compromise.
Both nominals are normally alike in definiteness, and the clarifier is a rigid rather than a derived nominal.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A verb preceding its subject does not copy the subject's plurality.
A verb preceding any plural subject takes feminine singular marking.
Feminine singular verb marking is permissible with a masculine broken plural subject in verb-first order.
Feminine singular is the grammarian-preferred option for a masculine plural subject in verb-first order.
Non-human plurals take feminine singular verbs, modifiers, and pronouns without exception.
When the subject precedes the verb, full plural agreement is required.
With a fronted verb over coordinated subjects, the verb agrees with the nearest conjunct.
A mixed-gender group resolves to masculine agreement across verbs, modifiers, and pronouns.
A post-verbal subject remains in the nominative.
Plural shape is irrelevant for non-human agreement but decisive for human agreement.

exceptions: mixed groups resolve to masculine rather than following the nearest conjunct once the subject precedes
